CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough for one week

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 74-year-old male who reports cough that started approximately one week ago. He has been bringing up yellow sputum. Symptoms have worsened over the last two days. Patient reports feeling warm but denies taking his temperature. Denies fevers and chills. Reports feeling achy at times. Denies shortness of breath. Reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and bilateral sinus pressure. Additionally, patient reports that while coughing earlier today, he fell down approximately 4-5 stairs and twisted his right knee. He has been able to walk since the fall but with a limp and pain on the inside of the knee. Denies feeling like the knee will give out. Reports able to bend and straighten the knee. Has taken over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief. No one else in the household is sick.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for cough with yellow sputum, nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, sinus pressure, and right knee pain. Denies fever, chills, shortness of breath. Denies new symptoms related to other systems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 milligrams daily
Metformin 1000 milligrams twice daily
Over-the-counter Dayquil

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as a teacher. Lives with wife. Denies smoking and alcohol use status not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood pressure 125/62 mmHg, Heart rate in the 80s, Oxygen saturation 97% on room air
Facial exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses
Nasal exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge
Throat exam: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space
Neck exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy
Lung exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough
Heart exam: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur
Right knee exam: Pain to palpation on right knee, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Upper respiratory infection with mild bronchitis: Viral syndrome. Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 milligrams twice daily. No antibiotics at this time. Patient instructed to call if symptoms worsen; chest x-ray may be ordered if symptoms do not improve.

2. Right knee pain: Right medial collateral ligament strain from fall. Prescribe meloxicam 15 milligrams once daily. Refer to physical therapy. Order right knee x-ray to rule out bone injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel. Patient counseled on importance of monitoring blood pressure and diet.

4. Diabetes mellitus: Continue metformin 1000 milligrams twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1c. Patient counseled on monitoring sugar intake and reporting blood sugars through patient portal to assess need for medication adjustment. Discussed potential complications of diabetes including kidney dysfunction and eye problems, emphasizing importance of diet management and monitoring.
